subject: Business Models
title: Pets.com: The Sock Puppet
description: Learn Pets.com: The Sock Puppet in one minute.

hook.text: Pets.com spent $12 million on a Super Bowl ad, sold dog food at a loss, and shut down in 268 days.

buildup.text: Pets.com shipped heavy, cheap pet supplies with free shipping. Every order lost money on fulfillment alone.

discovery.text: The company spent $12 selling each $1 of revenue. Its famous sock puppet mascot cost more than the products.

twist.text: Amazon invested in Pets.com, then launched its own pet section after watching the model fail. Amazon learned instead.

climax.text: Pets.com became the symbol of dot-com excess: great marketing, no viable economics.

punchline.text: $12 spent per $1 earned. The sock puppet was the most valuable asset.

quiz.question: What was Pets.com's fundamental business problem?
options: Shipping heavy cheap items at a loss on every order
